Chapter 10 • General Relativity

10.3 Coupling to Matter

Matter enters through its own action, added to \(S_\mathcal{D}\). Varying the matter fields gives their equations on the curved spacetime; varying the metric gives the Einstein equations with a source, the energy-momentum tensor. The Setting is that of Subsection 10.2.2.

  • Total action. For matter fields \(\Phi\) (tensor fields on \(\mathcal{M}\)) and a scalar field \(\mathcal{L}_M\) built from \(\Phi\), its derivatives and \(g\), \(S_M[g, \Phi] \coloneqq \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega^g \mathcal{L}_M\). The total action \(S_\mathcal{D} + S_M\) is required to be critical under two independent kinds of variations: of \(\Phi\) with \(g\) fixed, which give the matter field equations, and of \(g\) with \(\Phi\) fixed.

  • Energy-momentum tensor. The response of \(S_M\) to a change of the metric defines the symmetric \((0,2)\)-tensor field \(T\) (Landau and Lifshitz, 1975): \[ \boxed{ \frac{d}{d\textrm{\runic ᛊ}} S_M[g_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ}}, \Phi] \Big|_{\textrm{\runic ᛊ} = 0} = - \frac{1}{2} \int_\mathcal{D} \Omega^g \, (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}_{ij} , \qquad (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} = (g^{-1})^{ia} \, (g^{-1})^{jb} \, T_{ab} , } \] for every admissible \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\), uniquely by step 5. If \(\mathcal{L}_M\) contains no derivatives of \(g\), then \(\delta \mathcal{L}_M = \Theta^{ij} \, \textrm{\runic ᛉ}_{ij}\) with \(\Theta\) symmetric, and panel (A) of Figure 10.3 gives \[ (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} = - 2 \, \Theta^{ij} - \mathcal{L}_M \, (g^{-1})^{ij} , \] the second term coming from the volume element. Derivatives of \(g\) in \(\mathcal{L}_M\) are first moved off \(\textrm{\runic ᛉ}\) as in step 4.

  • Einstein equations. With \(- \kappa = 1/(16 \pi G_N)\), the variation of \(S_\mathcal{D} + S_M\) in \(g\) is \(\int_\mathcal{D} \Omega^g \big( \frac{1}{16 \pi G_N} (\hat{G})^{ij} - \frac{1}{2} (T^{\flat^{-1}})^{ij} \big) \textrm{\runic ᛉ}_{ij}\), and step 5 gives \[ \boxed{ G = 8 \pi G_N \, T . } \] \(T\) is to the metric what a current is to the electromagnetic potential: the response of the action to a change of it. The contracted Bianchi identity (Subsection B.18.10) forces \((g^{-1})^{kl} (\nabla_{\partial x_k} T)_{ln} = 0\), local conservation of energy and momentum, which a chart-independent \(\mathcal{L}_M\) guarantees through the matter field equations. The normalization of \(T\) gives the familiar energy densities and fluxes, and \(\mathrm{Ric}_{00} = 4 \pi G_N \rho\) of Chapter 9 in the Newtonian limit.

  • Example: electromagnetism. For the potential \(\mathsf{A}\), with \(F_{ij} = \partial_i \mathtt{a}_j - \partial_j \mathtt{a}_i\) and \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{EM}} = - \frac{1}{4} F_{ab} (F^{\flat^{-1}})^{ab}\), the two kinds of variations give the Einstein–Maxwell equations (Appendix in preparation) \[ G_{mn} = 8 \pi G_N \Big( - (g^{-1})^{bd} \, F_{mb} \, F_{nd} + \frac{1}{4} \, g_{mn} \, F_{ab} \, (F^{\flat^{-1}})^{ab} \Big), \qquad (\nabla_{\partial x_a} F^{\flat^{-1}})^{ab} = 0 . \]
